title: The Filter Pipeline
blurb: Inside MVC, filters wrap the action like an onion. They run in a fixed order — and people constantly confuse them with middleware. Order the five filter types.

docs.label: Microsoft Learn — Filters in ASP.NET Core

glossary.Authorization: Runs first. Decides if the request may proceed; can short-circuit everything else before any other filter runs.
glossary.Resource: Runs after authorization, before and after model binding. Good for caching or short-circuiting expensive work early.
glossary.Action: Wraps the action method itself — runs just before and just after your action executes.
glossary.Exception: Catches unhandled exceptions from the action (and action filters). Must sit so it can wrap the action's execution.
glossary.Result: Wraps execution of the ActionResult — runs just before and after the result (e.g. the JSON) is produced.

levels.title: L1 · The five filter types
levels.prompt: Order the filter types by when they first run as the request flows in. Hover each ⓘ if you're unsure.

failStates.title: Authorization goes first
failStates.explain: Authorization runs before everything else so it can reject an unauthorized request immediately — before any resource, action, or result work happens.

failStates.title: Resource wraps model binding
failStates.explain: Resource filters run around model binding, so they sit outside the action filters. Action filters are closer in — they wrap only the action method.

failStates.title: The result comes last
failStates.explain: Result filters wrap execution of the ActionResult, which happens after the action has returned. Result is the outermost-but-last step here.
